subject.title: fix(infra): make exec-approvals lock ownership filesystem-safe

question: Should this rebased PR become the sole canonical fix after it supplies exact-head VirtioFS proof, or should the related implementation at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 be refreshed and retained instead?
rationale: Both open PRs implement the same security-sensitive approach, while the available live evidence is attached to the related work rather than demonstrably to this current head; choosing one branch and the acceptable proof boundary is a maintainer ownership decision.

options.title: Require current-head runtime proof, then select this branch
options.body: Require a redacted Docker Desktop VirtioFS run against the rebased head that demonstrates repeated lock release and preserved fail-closed contention behavior before choosing it as the canonical PR.

options.title: Retain the related PR as canonical
options.body: Ask the related PR to rebase and refresh its evidence if its original author should retain ownership of the implementation path.

options.title: Pause both and define the lock contract first
options.body: Pause both PRs if maintainers want a shared `fs-safe` dependency fix or a different cross-process lock contract rather than an exec-approvals-local implementation.

recommendation.title: Require current-head runtime proof, then select this branch
recommendation.body: Require a redacted Docker Desktop VirtioFS run against the rebased head that demonstrates repeated lock release and preserved fail-closed contention behavior before choosing it as the canonical PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the live reproduction and authored the directly overlapping implementation, making them the best available technical routing contact for the proof and canonical-branch decision.
